central_node: Microbiology of Food, Preservation Techniques, and Human Digestion

key_details: Microscopic organisms like fungi (molds) and bacteria rot food
Thrive rapidly in warm, moist, and dark conditions
Spoiled food produces foul odor, bad taste, and cottony growth
real_world_examples: Greyish-white cottony mold growing on moist bread

key_details: Not all microbes cause illness or spoilage
Ferments warm milk into fresh curd without machinery
Gut microbes assist in human digestion
Removing water moisture inhibits microbial growth
Dry items resist spoilage for months
Sun heat evaporates water from food items
real_world_examples: Turning moist roti into dry khakhra

key_details: High salt concentration extracts water from microbial cells (osmosis)
Oil forms a surface layer that blocks atmospheric oxygen
Boiling uses high heat to destroy active microbes
real_world_examples: Pickling mangoes with salt, spices, and oil

key_details: Teeth chew food into smaller particles
Chewing increases food surface area for digestive enzymes
Saliva mixes with food to initiate chemical breakdown
